clue.text: Hold-up near Cork?

definitions.meaning: a narrow point where traffic or work gets jammed
the narrow top of a bottle sits right by its stopper, read cork as a stopper, not the Irish city

explanation.surface: A traffic jam somewhere close to the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' is capitalised to suggest the Irish city, but it is the stopper in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a congestion point delays things, and the narrow part of a bottle lies just below its stopper.

clue.text: Attempts, doesn't pass

definitions.meaning: in bridge or an auction, a player who makes an offer rather than passing

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying but never manages to pass a test.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge each player either makes a call or passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bids are tries at something, and someone who bids makes an offer at cards instead of passing.

clue.text: No relation of dead man?

parts.note: the proverb says dead men tell nothing, so a story or account (a relation) is what a dead man never gives

explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' looks like a family member but means a narrative; the saying is 'Dead men tell no tales'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a story, a relation in the sense of something recounted.

clue.text: Generous reception for political group

parts.note: liberal means generous or lavish
a reception is a party

explanation.surface: A lavish function is held for a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The Liberal Party was a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A UK political party, forerunner of today's Liberal Democrats.

clue.text: A girl, and not 11

parts.note: nor means and not
the academic award at 11 down is abbreviated MA

explanation.surface: A girl is introduced, and she is not the person at 11.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints '11', a cross-reference to the academic award at 11 down, abbreviated MA; the text file misread it as 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name, an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Becomes popular and gets the message

explanation.surface: Something becomes a hit and the meaning finally sinks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: a craze takes off, and a slow person finally understands.

clue.text: Notice in awkward situation

explanation.surface: Someone receives a formal notice that puts them in a tricky position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to catch sight of; a spot is also a predicament, as in being in a tight spot.

clue.text: Like official at university or in tropical parts

indicators.note: parts means splits up, so these letters are separated and reordered

explanation.surface: Something resembles a university officer, or bits of a hot country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges OR plus TROPICAL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proctors are disciplinary officers at Oxford and Cambridge, so this adjective describes them.

clue.text: Old riding school pupils of poor quality

definitions.meaning: travelling in the cheapest carriage on old British trains
children in the third form at school

explanation.surface: Students at a former riding school are not very good.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: British railways once had a cheapest third class, a school's third class is a year group, and third-class means inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: All three senses: old train travel at the lowest fare, a school year group, and something second-rate.

clue.text: Consider terribly idle, and tell off

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of idle are badly jumbled

parts.note: to tell off is to berate or scold

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a lazy person and gives them a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns IDLE into DELI; then add BERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to ponder or weigh something up at length.

clue.text: One wet area? Just the opposite

definitions.text: One wet area? Just the opposite

parts.words: One wet area? Just the opposite
parts.note: the reverse of a wet region is a parched one, a famous desert of Mongolia and China

explanation.walkthrough: The printed answer GORI is a misprint; the clue points to the opposite of a wet area, the Gobi Desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast arid desert, the very opposite of a damp region.

clue.text: Academic award for a smart set, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the phrase given might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A university degree given to a fashionable crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges all of FOR A SMART SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A university degree, commonly abbreviated MA.

clue.text: Benevolent, fundamentally, in excessive desire

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for excessive desire

parts.note: greed is excessive desire
fundamentally means at heart, deep down

explanation.surface: A kindly person whose generosity is, deep down, a kind of greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fundamentally' looks like an adverb on the definition, but it supplies the phrase meaning deep down; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone large-hearted is kind and generous, a benevolent soul.

clue.text: Following what French put in agreement

indicators.note: put in tells us the French word is inserted into the other

parts.note: consent is agreement
que is French for what

explanation.surface: Something comes after the French approve something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' signals the insertion; 'what French' means the French word for what.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequent means resulting, coming after as an effect.

clue.text: Book telling about extraordinary visions initially

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for telling wraps around the initials

parts.note: a relation is a telling or account

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A book recounting some extraordinary visions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling' looks like a verb describing the book but is a noun, an account; 'initially' and 'about' are the selection and container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation is the final book of the New Testament, full of apocalyptic visions.

clue.text: Supreme bosses for some cricket ground

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls, a portion of a cricket game
Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Top executives pay for a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground; an OVER is a unit of six balls in cricket. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers with authority over others, the highest bosses.

clue.text: Lets hope triumph over experience, in Johnson's view

definitions.text: Lets hope triumph over experience, in Johnson's view

parts.words: Lets hope triumph over experience, in Johnson's view
parts.note: Samuel Johnson called a second wedding the triumph of hope over experience

explanation.walkthrough: Dr Johnson, the 18th-century English writer, said a man marrying again showed 'the triumph of hope over experience'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who weds again lets hope win out over past experience, per Johnson.

clue.text: A couple of learners in Austria

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Two trainee drivers are on holiday in Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The two learners are TYRO (a novice) and L (the British L-plate on a learner driver's car). The definition is a place found in Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region lying largely in western Austria.

clue.text: Italian city that has another name for colour

indicators.note: the city name plus another of the letter gives the colour, so the colour loses one

parts.note: sienna is a brownish earth colour

explanation.surface: A Tuscan city which also gives its name to a paint colour.
explanation.walkthrough: SIENNA, the colour, has one more N than SIENA, the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a historic city in Tuscany, central Italy.

clue.text: Youngster preserves islanders

parts.note: a minor is someone underage
to can is to preserve food in tins

explanation.surface: A youngster is protecting some island inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserves' looks like a verb meaning protects, but it gives CANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Balearic island of Menorca are known by this name.

clue.text: Pity workers producing out-of-date weapon

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy, or pity, to a foe
staff are a company's workers

explanation.surface: Sympathetic employees turn out an antiquated arm.
explanation.walkthrough: QUARTER is mercy shown to a defeated enemy. 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden pole once used as a fighting weapon in England, now obsolete.

clue.text: Right call winner gets at Wimbledon, for instance

definitions.text: winner gets at Wimbledon, for instance
definitions.meaning: the championship won at the tennis tournament

explanation.surface: Correctly calling the result of a Wimbledon match.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim, a name to call by, and a sporting championship.

clue.text: It may be said to insult a horse

definitions.text: It may be said to insult

definitions.meaning: a hardy breed from North Africa's Barbary coast

explanation.surface: A remark that might offend a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed HARB is a misprint for BARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a wounding jibe, and the Barbary breed of horse.

clue.text: Colourless limit of proper behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone goes white at the limits of decent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond the pale' means outside acceptable conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: lacking colour, and a fenced boundary beyond which conduct is unacceptable.

clue.text: Country turned into this large lake

indicators.note: turned says the letters of the country's name are rearranged

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A nation is transformed into a great body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' swaps letters in EIRE, the Irish name for Ireland. 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Great Lakes of North America, on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Old stuff about to be included in new variation

indicators.note: to be included in signals one piece put inside another
new suggests the letters of variation are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Antiques are to be part of a fresh version of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns VARIATION into VITORIANA; 'to be included in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects from the nineteenth-century era of the queen, now collectibles.

clue.text: Wine Paul made originally

definitions.meaning: a deep red Spanish wine, chiefly used for sacrament
St Paul was a tentmaker by trade, according to Acts

explanation.surface: A wine that was first produced by someone called Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the apostle, who made his living as a tentmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dark Spanish red wine, and the canvas shelter St Paul crafted for a living.

clue.text: Professed to be less in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means scattered, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be less disorganised than they really are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' rearranges TO BE LESS IN; the 'in' is fodder, not part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or declared, as a professed reason may hide the real one.
